newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine capital launches bond program.
newsitem.headline: Argentine capital launches bond program.

text.p: Argentina's city of Buenos Aires presented Monday the launch of a bond program which will sharply reduce the capital city's debt servicing charges by cancelling old debt.
Officials from the city presented the program, which includes the placment of $250 million of 10-year bonds and 250 million pesos of five or seven year bonds in the international capital markets.
The officials said the city is planning a roadshow to the United States and Europe to promote the bonds which will be placed on March 14. Chase Manhattan International Limited is the lead manager.

Adalberto Rodriguez Giavarini, the city's secretary of finance said the issue is aimed at lengthening the debt maturities of the city, reducing debt costs by paying off more costly loans and allow the capital to have more flexible financing.

"The implementation of this program was planned since the beginning of this administration's term in office, to improve the fiscal situation inherited from past administrations, which had poor savings, high levels of budgetary expenditure and delayed payments to suppliers," said Giavarini.
According to the city, debt interest will be reduced to 11 percent from 15.6 percent through the issuance of the bonds.

Some 246.8 million of the funds raised through the issues will be used to cancel debt with state-owned Banco de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires. A further $50 million will pay-off other bank debts, $100.5 million will be used to pay off debt with suppliers and $100 million will be used to recapitalize Banco de la Ciudad.
